_open_questions: Delay display step: the unit holds delay in steps of 1/384 ms at 96 kHz (about 2.6 us), up to 12 ms. Whether the vendor's software offers that resolution or rounds it to a coarser entry step is not checked, so `step_ms` records the held step, not necessarily the entry step.
EQ gain range and step: not recorded. The stored value can hold finer steps than 0.25 dB, but what the software lets a user type is unknown.
Presets: the unit holds 4. Whether the input selection switches with the preset is not checked, so check the input after every preset switch until it is.

Input EQ and group EQ: both exist on this unit and are not a tier in this profile yet. Their channel mapping is not settled, which is why `groups_enumerated` is false and `fields` of the one listed tier says nothing about them.

Crossover families: Chebyshev, and Bessel at 6 / 18 / 24 dB/oct, are taken from the contributor's reading of the vendor's filter tables and have not been compared with a preset saved by the vendor's software. The corner and Q factors are tabulated there, but Chebyshev ripple is not stated in this profile.

Odd-order Linkwitz (6 and 18 dB/oct) is a vendor menu label, not a true Linkwitz-Riley alignment: the 18 dB/oct leg is a 1st-order section plus a 2nd-order Q 0.707 section, and the 6 dB/oct leg is a 1st-order section with its corner scaled. Their phase behaviour is unmeasured.

Peak-EQ bandwidth convention: the software has two ways to turn f / Q / gain into a peak, one standard constant-Q and one where the bandwidth depends on gain. The setting is not stored in a preset, so the same numbers give a different curve in each. Which one the owner's software is set to must be asked before an EQ is proposed.
Acoustic check: the filters were compared with presets saved by the vendor's software, not with a loopback measurement of the unit's output.

channel_gain.note: Level per output, 0.5 dB steps. A muted output keeps its set level.

crossover_filters.slope_range_note: Each leg is one or two biquad sections at 96 kHz: 6 dB/oct is one 1st-order section, 12 one 2nd-order, 18 a 1st plus a 2nd, 24 two 2nd-order. The families differ in section Q and corner factor. The unit also has a global corner-correction setting (off, -3 dB or -6 dB normalised) that shifts the corner factors; its state is not part of a preset's crossover fields and must be asked.

delay.step_ms_note: The held resolution, 1/384 ms (2.604 us) at 96 kHz. The step the software shows is unverified (see _open_questions).

dsp_profile.dsp_processing_rate_note: The unit processes at 96 kHz; delays in samples derive from it.

CHEBYSHEV.modellable_note: CHEBYSHEV is not in the method's default realisable set (dsp_math.MODELLABLE_FAMILIES) — ENTERABLE on this device, not predictable by us

groups.label: Output channels
groups.note: Six amplified channels and two line outputs. The unit also has an input EQ and a group EQ (shared left/right bands per output group); they are not listed as a tier here yet, and their mapping is not settled.

dsp_profile.name: PICO 6/8-2 DSP

polarity.implementation: 0 / 180 degree switch per output; no continuous all-pass phase control apart from the APF1 / APF2 EQ bands

presets.note: Check the input after every preset switch until it is known whether the input selection follows the preset.
